name: Time
description: Time

name: Depth
description: Depth is the vertical distance below the surface.

name: Longitude
description: Longitude is positive eastward; its units of degree_east (or equivalent) indicate this explicitly. In a latitude-longitude system defined with respect to a rotated North Pole, the standard name of grid_longitude should be used instead of longitude. Grid longitude is positive in the grid-eastward direction, but its units should be plain degree.

name: Latitude
description: Latitude is positive northward; its units of degree_north (or equivalent) indicate this explicitly. In a latitude-longitude system defined with respect to a rotated North Pole, the standard name of grid_latitude should be used instead of latitude. Grid latitude is positive in the grid-northward direction, but its units should be plain degree.

name: Water temperature
description: Lake water temperature is the in situ temperature of the lake water. To specify the depth at which the temperature applies use a vertical coordinate variable or scalar coordinate variable. There are standard names for lake_surface_temperature, lake_surface_skin_temperature, lake_surface_subskin_temperature and lake_surface_foundation_temperature which can be used to describe data located at the specified surfaces.

name: Air Temperature
description: Air temperature

name: Wind Speed
description: Speed is the magnitude of velocity. Wind is defined as a two-dimensional (horizontal) air velocity vector, with no vertical component. (Vertical motion in the atmosphere has the standard name upward_air_velocity.) The wind speed is the magnitude of the wind velocity.

name: Wind Direction
description: Wind is defined as a two-dimensional (horizontal) air velocity vector, with no vertical component. (Vertical motion in the atmosphere has the standard name upward_air_velocity.) In meteorological reports, the direction of the wind vector is usually (but not always) given as the direction from which it is blowing (wind_from_direction) (westerly, northerly, etc.). In other contexts, such as atmospheric modelling, it is often natural to give the direction in the usual manner of vectors as the heading or the direction to which it is blowing (wind_to_direction) (eastward, southward, etc.) "from_direction" is used in the construction X_from_direction and indicates the direction from which the velocity vector of X is coming.

name: Rainfall
description: "Amount" means mass per unit area. The construction thickness_of_[X_]rainfall_amount means the accumulated "depth" of rainfall i.e. the thickness of a layer of liquid water having the same mass per unit area as the rainfall amount.

name: Air Pressure
description: Air pressure is the force per unit area which would be exerted when the moving gas molecules of which the air is composed strike a theoretical surface of any orientation.

name: Solar Irradiance
description: The quantity with standard name solar_irradiance, often called Total Solar Irradiance (TSI), is the radiation from the sun integrated over the whole electromagnetic spectrum and over the entire solar disk. The quantity applies outside the atmosphere, by default at a distance of one astronomical unit from the sun, but a coordinate or scalar coordinate variable of distance_from_sun can be used to specify a value other than the default. "Irradiance" means the power per unit area (called radiative flux in other standard names), the area being normal to the direction of flow of the radiant energy.

name: Dissolved Oxygen
description: Dissolved oxygen refers to the level of free, non-compound oxygen present in water or other liquids.

name: PAR
description: Designates the spectral range (wave band) of solar radiation from 400 to 700 nanometers that photosynthetic organisms are able to use in the process of photosynthesis.

name: pH
description: A figure expressing the acidity or alkalinity of a solution on a logarithmic scale on which 7 is neutral, lower values are more acid and higher values more alkaline. The pH is equal to −log10 c, where c is the hydrogen ion concentration in moles per litre.

name: Chlorophyll A
description: 'Mass concentration' means mass per unit volume and is used in the construction mass_concentration_of_X_in_Y, where X is a material constituent of Y. A chemical or biological species denoted by X may be described by a single term such as 'nitrogen' or a phrase such as 'nox_expressed_as_nitrogen'. Chlorophylls are the green pigments found in most plants, algae and cyanobacteria; their presence is essential for photosynthesis to take place. There are several different forms of chlorophyll that occur naturally. All contain a chlorin ring (chemical formula C20H16N4) which gives the green pigment and a side chain whose structure varies. The naturally occurring forms of chlorophyll contain between 35 and 55 carbon atoms. Chlorophyll-a is the most commonly occurring form of natural chlorophyll. The chemical formula of chlorophyll-a is C55H72O5N4Mg.

name: Turbidity
description: Turbidity is a dimensionless quantity which is expressed in NTU (Nephelometric Turbidity Units). Turbidity expressed in NTU is the proportion of white light scattered back to a transceiver by the particulate load in a body of water, represented on an arbitrary scale referenced against measurements made in the laboratory on aqueous suspensions of formazine beads.

name: Conductivity
description: Electrical conductivity (EC) estimates the amount of total dissolved salts (TDS), or the total amount of dissolved ions in the water.

name: Water Pressure
description: "Water pressure" is the pressure that exists in the medium water. It includes the pressure due to overlying water, air and any other medium that may be present.

name: Water Velocity Northward
description: A velocity is a vector quantity. "Northward" indicates a vector component which is positive when directed northward (negative southward).

name: Water Velocity Eastward
description: A velocity is a vector quantity. "Eastward" indicates a vector component which is positive when directed eastward (negative westward).

name: Water Velocity Vertical
description: A velocity is a vector quantity. "Vertical" indicates a vector component which is positive when directed upwards (negative downwards).

name: Oxygen Saturation
description: Fractional saturation is the ratio of some measure of concentration to the saturated value of the same quantity.

name: Total Suspended Matter
description: Total Suspended Solids (TSS) refers to any particles that are suspended in the water column. These particles can include silt, algae, sediment, and other solids floating in the water (both organic and inorganic). These particles are defined as being large enough to not pass through the filter (through the filtration process) used to separate them from the water.

name: Relative Humidity
description: Relative humidity (RH) is the ratio of the partial pressure of water vapor to the equilibrium vapor pressure of water at a given temperature. Relative humidity depends on temperature and the pressure of the system of interest. The same amount of water vapor results in higher relative humidity in cool air than warm air. A related parameter is the dew point.

name: Water Velocity
description: A velocity is a vector quantity. This is composed of a northern and eastern component.

name: Range
description: Vertical distance of each data bin from the acoustic current profilers transducer

name: Binary Error Mask
description: data_binary_mask has 1 where condition X is met, 0 elsewhere. 0 = high quality, 1 = low quality.

name: Standard Deviation
description: A measure of the amount of variation or dispersion of a set of values

name: Water Velocity Magnitude
description: The magnitude of Northern and Eastern velocity vectors.

name: Water Velocity Lateral Direction
description: The direction of Northern and Eastern velocity vectors.

name: Backscattering
description: Scattering of radiation is its deflection from its incident path without loss of energy. Backwards scattering refers to the sum of scattering into all backward angles i.e. scattering_angle exceeding pi/2 radians. A scattering_angle should not be specified with this quantity.

name: Net Surface Heat Flux
description: Heat flux or thermal flux, sometimes also referred to as heat flux density, heat-flow density or heat flow rate intensity is a flow of energy per unit of area per unit of time. In SI its units are watts per square metre (W/m2). It has both a direction and a magnitude, and so it is a vector quantity. To define the heat flux at a certain point in space, one takes the limiting case where the size of the surface becomes infinitesimally small.

name: Wind Stress
description: In physical oceanography and fluid dynamics, the wind stress is the shear stress exerted by the wind on the surface of large bodies of water – such as oceans, seas, estuaries and lakes. It is the force component parallel to the surface, per unit area, as applied by the wind on the water surface.

name: Shear Velocity on Water
description: Shear Velocity, also called friction velocity, is a form by which a shear stress may be re-written in units of velocity. It is useful as a method in fluid mechanics to compare true velocities, such as the velocity of a flow in a stream, to a velocity that relates shear between layers of flow.

name: Surface Buoyancy Flux
description: Surface Buoyancy Flux

name: Salinity
description: Salinity is the saltiness or amount of salt dissolved in a body of water, called saline water.

name: Potential Redox
description: Redox potential (also known as reduction / oxidation potential, 'ROP', pe, ε, or. ) is a measure of the tendency of a chemical species to acquire electrons from or lose electrons to an electrode and thereby be reduced or oxidised respectively.

name: Phycoerythrin
description: Phycoerythrin is a red protein-pigment complex from the light-harvesting phycobiliprotein family, present in red algae and cryptophytes, accessory to the main chlorophyll pigments responsible for photosynthesis.

name: Phycocyanin
description: Phycocyanin is a pigment-protein complex from the light-harvesting phycobiliprotein family, along with allophycocyanin and phycoerythrin. It is an accessory pigment to chlorophyll.

name: Primary Production
description: Primary production is the production of chemical energy in organic compounds by living organisms. The main source of this energy is sunlight but a minute fraction of primary production is driven by lithotrophic organisms using the chemical energy of inorganic molecules.

name: Secchi Depth
description: A Secchi disk is a metal disk, 8 inches in diameter that is lowered into the water on a cord. The depth that the Secchi disk can no longer be seen through the water is the Secchi depth. When the water transparency is high, the Secchi depth is high.

name: Conductivity (20degC)
description: Electrical conductivity (EC) estimates the amount of total dissolved salts (TDS), or the total amount of dissolved ions in the water. This is normalized to 20 degC.

name: Downwelling irradiance
description: Downwelling short-wave radiation at the surface has a component due to the direct solar beam, and a diffuse component scattered from atmospheric constituents and reflected from clouds.

name: kd
description: Diffuse Attenuation Coefficient of Downwelling Irradiance

name: Dew Point
description: The dew point is the temperature the air needs to be cooled to (at constant pressure) in order to achieve a relative humidity (RH) of 100%. At this point the air cannot hold more water in the gas form.

name: Air Pressure Mean Sea Level
description: Air pressure corrected to mean sea level. Air pressure is the force per unit area which would be exerted when the moving gas molecules of which the air is composed strike a theoretical surface of any orientation.

name: Wind Speed Gust
description: Gusts are the peak wind speed. Speed is the magnitude of velocity. Wind is defined as a two-dimensional (horizontal) air velocity vector, with no vertical component. (Vertical motion in the atmosphere has the standard name upward_air_velocity.) The wind speed is the magnitude of the wind velocity.

name: Epilimnion Temperature
description: Average temperature of the surface mixed layer

name: Bottom temperature
description: Water temperature at the deepest measurement point

name: Stratification Onset
description: Onset of lake stratification in spring/summer

name: Stratification Duration
description: Duration of summer stratification

name: Stratification Termination
description: Termination of summer stratification

name: Morphology
description: Morphology

name: Duration of ice cover
description: Duration of ice cover

name: Ice Off
description: End of ice cover

name: Ice On
description: Start of ice cover

name: Density
description: Density, mass of a unit volume of a material substance. The formula for density is d = M/V, where d is density, M is mass, and V is volume. Density is commonly expressed in units of grams per cubic centimetre.

name: Potential Temperature
description: The potential temperature of a parcel of fluid at pressure P is the temperature that the parcel would attain if adiabatically brought to a standard reference pressure P0, usually 1,000 hPa (1,000 mb).

name: Potential Density
description: The potential density of a fluid parcel at pressure P is the density that the parcel would acquire if adiabatically brought to a reference pressure P0, often 1 bar (100 kPa).

name: Thorpe Displacements
description: TBD

name: Surface temperature
description: Temperature of the top-most sensor

name: Mixing depth
description: mixing depth calculated using temperature

name: Daily maximum mixing depth
description: Daily maximum of mixing depth (calculated using temperature)

name: Wave Direction
description: Direction of waves

name: Water Velocity Cross-Shore
description: Projected Cross-shore water velocity

name: Monin Obukhov length
description: The Obukhov length (L) measures the relative importance of mechanical shear-generated turbulence and density-driven (buoyancy) fluxes

name: Water Velocity Along-Shore
description: Projected along-shore water velocity

name: Heading
description: Direction of instrument

name: Roll
description: Roll of the instrument

name: Pitch
description: Pitch of the instrument

name: Vapor Pressure
description: The equilibrium vapor pressure is an indication of a liquid's evaporation rate. It relates to the tendency of particles to escape from the liquid (or a solid).

name: Surface dissolved oxygen
description: Dissolved oxygen at the lake surface

name: Bottom dissolved oxygen
description: Dissolved oxygen at the lake bottom

name: Hypolimnetic oxygen
description: Oxygen mass below 15 m depth

name: Fluorescence
description: Indirect measure of pigment concentration

name: Water depth
description: Depth of lake at mooring location
